stem: Mira received `assets-0.9.tar.gz` and wants to see which files are inside before unpacking it. Which `tar` option lists an archive’s contents? Type the option with its dash, short or long form.
explanation: `-t` (long form `--list`) lists an archive’s members without extracting them. With `-f` naming the file and `-z` for gzip, the full command is `tar -ztf assets-0.9.tar.gz`; `-x` would extract instead.

stem: Ada wants one gzip-compressed file, `release-0.9.tar.gz`, that holds the folder `assets`. Which command does that?
explanation: Create mode (`-c`), gzip filter (`-z`) and the file name (`-f`, written last in the group) give the `.tar.gz`. Keep `-f` right before the archive’s name.

options.rationale: `-f` takes the next word as the archive name, so `tar` would create a file called `z` and treat the rest as input.
`-x` extracts from an existing archive; it never creates one.
`-c` creates the archive, `-z` filters it through gzip, and `-f` is followed by the archive’s name.
`gzip` compresses single files and does not bundle a folder into an archive.

stem: Mira received `backup.tar` and wants to see which files it holds before she unpacks anything. Which command shows them?
explanation: Listing with `-t` first shows where the files will land and whether the archive holds one tidy folder or many loose files.

options.rationale: `-t` prints the table of contents without writing any files.
`-x` unpacks the files into the current directory instead of just listing them.
`-c` would create a new archive, overwriting this one with an archive of nothing.
`-v` only makes another mode talkative; on its own it names no mode, so `tar` refuses to run.

stem: Jonas wants a `.tar.bz2` file. Which `tar` option selects the bzip2 compressor?
explanation: The three filters are `-z` for gzip, `-j` for bzip2 and `-J` for xz. Mind the capital letter for xz.

options.rationale: `-z` selects gzip, which makes a `.tar.gz`.
`-x` is the extract mode; it chooses no compressor.
`tar` has no `-b` option for bzip2 (its `-b` sets a block size).
`-j` filters the archive through bzip2.

stem: Mira runs `tar -xzf release.tar.gz -C /tmp/check`. What does the `-C /tmp/check` part do?
explanation: `-C DIR` is how you unpack into another directory. Without it, `tar` extracts into the directory you are in.

options.text: It compresses with the fastest setting
options.rationale: Speed is not chosen with `-C`; the compressor comes from `-z`, `-j` or `-J`.

options.text: It changes into `/tmp/check` first, so the files are extracted there
options.rationale: `-C` means “change directory”; the target directory must already exist.
The archive is named after `-f`, and `-x` extracts, so nothing is created.

options.text: It checks the archive against the files in `/tmp/check`
options.rationale: `tar` has no such check with `-C`; the option only changes directory.

stem: Mira runs `gzip notes.txt` in a folder that holds only that file. What does the folder contain afterwards?
explanation: The compressors `gzip`, `bzip2` and `xz` all replace the original unless you add `-k`.

options.rationale: By default `gzip` replaces the file with its compressed version.
The original is kept only with `-k` (keep).
`gzip` writes a new `.gz` file and removes the original; the name never stays the same.
`gzip` makes no backup copy.

stem: Which statement about `tar -cf sprites.tar assets/sprites`, with no compression option, is true?
explanation: Archiving and compression are separate jobs. The ending `.tar` says “bundled”; `.tar.gz` says “bundled, then compressed with gzip”.

options.text: It compresses every file with gzip by default
options.rationale: GNU `tar` only compresses when you add `-z`, `-j`, `-J` or a similar filter.

options.text: It deletes the original files after bundling them
options.rationale: `tar` leaves the originals in place unless you ask it to remove them.

options.text: It bundles the files into one archive but does not make them smaller
options.rationale: Archiving only collects files and their paths into one file; compression is a separate step.

options.text: It can only bundle a single file at a time
options.rationale: Several files and whole directories can go into one archive.

stem: Jonas must send the folder `screenshots` to colleagues on Windows as one ZIP file. Which command creates it?
explanation: ZIP is the format that Windows and macOS open natively. `zip` creates the archive and compresses each file inside it, but a directory needs `-r`.

options.rationale: Without `-r`, `zip` stores only the empty directory entry, not the files inside.
`-r` makes `zip` go into the folder and store everything below it.
This creates a gzip-compressed tar file that merely carries the name `.zip`; Windows tools won’t open it as ZIP.
`gzip` treats the first word as a file to compress and does not build ZIP archives.

stem: Which command lists the files inside `assets.zip` without extracting them?
explanation: `unzip` extracts by default, so use `-l` when you only want to see what is inside.

options.rationale: `-d` names a directory to extract into; the command would then try to extract with a wrong name.
`-x` excludes the files that follow it from extraction, and the command would still extract.
`zip` creates and updates archives; its `-l` option converts line endings in the files it adds.
`-l` lists the archive’s members, much like `tar -t` does for tar files.

stem: Ada sees a file called `levels-pack.tar.xz`. What does the name say about it?
explanation: Endings are only a convention, but they tell the next person how to unpack the file. The `file` command shows what the content really is.

options.text: A ZIP archive with extra-strong compression
options.rationale: ZIP files end in `.zip`; the `.xz` ending belongs to the xz compressor.

options.text: A tar archive that was then compressed with gzip
options.rationale: `.gz` is the ending for gzip; xz files end in `.xz`.

options.text: A tar archive that was then compressed with xz
options.rationale: The endings read left to right in the order the steps were done: tar bundled, xz compressed.

options.text: An xz file that tar later bundled again
options.rationale: The last ending shows the last step, and that is the compression.

stem: Mira has `fight.log.gz` and wants the original `fight.log` back, with the `.gz` file removed. Which command does that?
explanation: The matching commands are `gunzip`, `bunzip2` and `unxz`. They are the same as `gzip -d`, `bzip2 -d` and `xz -d`.

options.rationale: `gunzip` decompresses a `.gz` file and, by default, removes it afterwards.
This tries to compress a file that already has the `.gz` ending and leaves it unchanged.
`tar` unpacks archives; this file is a single compressed log, not a tar archive.
`unzip` reads ZIP files, not the gzip format.

stem: Ada archives old logs that nobody reads and she does not mind the extra time. Which `tar` option usually produces the smallest result?
explanation: As a rule of thumb gzip is fastest and biggest, bzip2 sits in the middle, and xz is slowest and smallest.

options.rationale: gzip is the fastest of the three, but it usually leaves the largest file.
bzip2 compresses harder than gzip but usually not as hard as xz.
`-c` creates an archive; it does not choose a compressor.
xz usually squeezes hardest, though it is the slowest of the three to compress.

stem: Which of these commands fails with the message that `assets` is a directory and is ignored?
explanation: That is why `tar` exists: bundle the folder into one file first, then compress it. `tar -czf` does both steps in one command.

options.rationale: `tar` bundles directories without trouble.
`gzip` compresses single files only, so it skips a directory.
With `-r`, `zip` stores the folder and all files below it.
This bundles the folder and compresses the bundle in one go.

stem: Ada must unpack `release.tar.gz` into the existing folder `/tmp/check`, not into her current folder. Which command does that?
explanation: To choose where files land, use `-C DIR` (the directory must already exist). Without it, files are written below the current directory.

options.rationale: `-x` extracts, `-z` handles gzip, and `-C` changes into the target directory first.
A word after the archive name is a member to extract, so `tar` would look for a file called `/tmp/check` inside the archive.
`-c` creates an archive, overwriting `release.tar.gz` instead of unpacking it.
`-t` only lists the members; nothing is written anywhere.

stem: Mira needs one compressed file that holds the whole folder `assets`. Which commands create it? (Choose TWO.)
explanation: Only `tar` with `-c` and a compression option, or `zip -r`, handles a folder. The single-file compressors need a tar archive first.

options.rationale: `gzip` refuses directories and says it is ignoring them.
It bundles the folder into a tar archive and compresses it with gzip.
`bzip2` also works on single files only.
`-t` lists an existing archive and creates nothing.
It creates a ZIP archive and compresses each file inside it.

stem: Which `tar` options select a compression program? (Choose THREE.)
explanation: Remember the trio `z`, `j` and `J`: gzip, bzip2 and xz.

options.rationale: Selects gzip.
It changes the directory; it has nothing to do with compression.
Selects bzip2.
It lists files as `tar` works; the result is unchanged.
It lists the archive’s table of contents.
Selects xz.

stem: Which statements about `gzip`, `bzip2` and `xz` are true? (Choose TWO.)
explanation: Remember the pattern: one file in, one compressed file out, original removed unless you add `-k`.

options.text: They can compress a whole directory when given `-r`
options.rationale: Directories are handled by `tar` or `zip -r`, not by these three.

options.text: They all produce files that end in `.zip`
options.rationale: The endings are `.gz`, `.bz2` and `.xz`.

options.text: `xz` is the fastest of the three
options.rationale: It is usually the slowest; gzip is the fastest.

options.text: Each one works on a single file and, by default, replaces it with the compressed version
options.rationale: The original disappears unless you ask to keep it.

options.text: `-k` keeps the original file next to the compressed one
options.rationale: It stands for “keep”.

stem: Which commands list the contents of an archive without extracting it? (Choose TWO.)
explanation: Listing first is a good habit: `tar -t` and `unzip -l` show the paths before you write anything.

options.rationale: The `-t` mode prints the members of the archive.
The `-l` option lists the members of a ZIP file.
`-x` writes the files to disk.
Without `-l`, `unzip` extracts.
It decompresses the file and removes the `.gz` ending; it does not list anything.

stem: Mira wants only `assets/README.md` out of `assets-0.9.tar.gz`. Complete the command so it extracts that one file into the current directory.
explanation: Name the member after the archive. `-x` extracts, `-f` names the archive, and `-z` is optional when reading, because GNU `tar` detects gzip itself.

stem: Which option makes `gzip` keep the original file instead of deleting it? Type the short option with its dash.
explanation: `-k` (long form `--keep`) leaves the original in place, so you end up with both `fight.log` and `fight.log.gz`.

stem: Type a command that decompresses `fight.log.gz` and removes the `.gz` file again.
explanation: `gunzip` is the same program as `gzip -d`. Both turn `fight.log.gz` back into `fight.log`.

stem: Which long or short option tells `tar` to use xz when creating an archive? Type it with its dashes.
explanation: A capital `-J` (long form `--xz`) filters through xz and goes with the `.tar.xz` ending.

stem: Complete the command so it creates `assets.zip` from the folder `assets`, including every file below it.
explanation: The directory needs `-r` (recursive); the archive’s name comes before the files to add.

stem: Which `unzip` option extracts the archive into another directory, here `out`? Type the option with its dash.
explanation: `-d DIR` sets the extraction directory, like `-C` does for `tar`.

verify.command: zip -rq a.zip assets; mkdir out; unzip -q a.zip {answer} out

stem: The release script made `assets-0.9.tar.gz`. How many lines does this command print? Type the number.
explanation: `tar -tf` lists one member per line, folders included, and `wc -l` counts those lines. The folder entries are why the number is bigger than the number of regular files.

stem: Mira archives one subfolder and lists the result. What is printed?
explanation: `tar` keeps each name as typed on the command line and adds the directory entry before its files.

options.rationale: The folder itself is a member of the archive too, so it appears as its own line.
`tar` stores the paths exactly as given, so the `assets/` part stays.
The directory entry comes first, then the two files below it, all with the paths given on the command line.
The archive does not contain itself; `-t` shows only what is inside it.

stem: What does the listing show after `gzip -k` ran inside `assets`?
explanation: `gzip -k` keeps the original, so both files exist afterwards. `ls -1` prints one name per line.

options.rationale: Without `-k` this would be right, because the original is removed.
`-k` keeps README.md and adds README.md.gz; `ls` sorts the names, ignoring case.
This is the folder before compressing; the new `.gz` file is missing.
Uppercase names would come first only with the plain C locale; here `ls` sorts ignoring case, so `levels` is listed before `README.md`.

stem: Type the one line this prints.
explanation: The archive stores paths starting with `assets/`, so extracting into `out` creates `out/assets`. Only that one folder sits directly in `out`.
command:
mkdir out
tar -xzf assets-0.9.tar.gz -C out
ls -1 out

stem: What does the `file` command report for this archive?
explanation: `file` looks at the real content, not the name, so it shows which compressor was used.
output: a.tar.xz: XZ compressed data, checksum CRC64

options.text: a.tar.xz: gzip compressed data, from Unix
options.rationale: That is what `-z` would produce. A capital `-J` selects xz.

options.text: a.tar.xz: bzip2 compressed data, block size = 900k
options.rationale: bzip2 comes from `-j`, not `-J`.
That would be a plain uncompressed tar, which needs no filter option.

options.text: a.tar.xz: XZ compressed data, checksum CRC64
options.rationale: `-J` made an xz-compressed archive, and `file` identifies that from the content.

stem: Type the one line this prints.
explanation: `gzip` replaces `all.tar` with `all.tar.gz`, so the glob `all*` matches only the compressed file.
command:
tar -cf all.tar assets
gzip all.tar
ls -1 all*

stem: Ada archives an absolute path with `tar -cf logs.tar /var/log/syslog`. What does `tar` do with the leading slash of the member name?
explanation: GNU `tar` protects against overwriting system files on extraction by storing relative names, and it tells you so.

options.text: It keeps the slash, so extraction always writes to `/var/log/syslog`.
options.rationale: That only happens with `-P`.

options.text: It refuses the path and exits without making an archive.
options.rationale: Absolute paths are accepted; only the stored name changes.

options.text: It removes the slash, prints a notice, and stores `var/log/syslog`.
options.rationale: The notice reads "Removing leading `/' from member names".

options.text: It replaces the slash with `~`, so the file lands in the home directory.
options.rationale: `tar` never rewrites a name this way.

stem: Which `tar` option keeps the leading `/` of absolute file names in the archive?
explanation: The option is the capital letter; the default removes the slash.

options.rationale: `-P` (`--absolute-names`) stores names exactly as given.
`-C` changes the directory before working.
`-v` only lists files while working.
`-J` selects xz compression.

stem: Jonas runs `tar -rf backup.tar.gz notes.txt` to add one more file. What happens?
explanation: Appending and updating need a plain archive, because a compressed stream can't be extended in place.

options.text: `tar` appends the file and recompresses the archive.
options.rationale: It never recompresses for you.

options.text: `tar` appends the file and leaves the gzip layer as it was.
options.rationale: That would corrupt the archive, so `tar` refuses.

options.text: `tar` replaces the whole archive with one that holds only `notes.txt`.
options.rationale: Nothing is overwritten; the command just fails.

options.text: `tar` stops with the error "Cannot update compressed archives".
options.rationale: `-r` and `-u` work only on uncompressed `.tar` files.

stem: Which statement about the numbered levels of `gzip` is correct?
explanation: Levels trade time against size; the default sits in the middle.

options.text: `-1` compresses best and `-9` is the fastest.
options.rationale: It is the other way round.

options.text: `-1` is fastest but compresses least; `-9` is slowest but compresses most.
options.rationale: A higher level spends more time to save more space.

options.text: The level decides which file ending `gzip` adds.
options.rationale: The ending is always `.gz`.

options.text: A level of `-0` stores the file in a ZIP archive.
options.rationale: `gzip` has no `-0` level and does not make ZIP files.

stem: Jonas wants `zip` to store his files without compressing them at all. Which option does he use?
explanation: ZIP levels run from none to maximum.

options.rationale: Level 1 compresses, but as fast as possible.
Level 9 compresses as much as possible.
`-r` makes `zip` descend into directories.
Level 0 only stores the files.

stem: Mira wants to read `build.log.gz` on screen without unpacking it. Which command does that?
explanation: `zcat` decompresses to standard output and leaves the `.gz` file alone.

options.rationale: That lists archive members, and a `.gz` log is not a tar archive.
`zip` does not read gzip files.
It prints the decompressed text and keeps the file.
That tries to compress it again.
